sentences: Scientists have estimated how many colors we can see and how many scents we can smell … but director John Lloyd can’t find anyone who has counted how many sounds we can hear.
Drawing on a legendary career in radio, film and TV, he makes a funny case for paying closer attention to sound — and for listening more than you talk.
(Plus: find out why almost every frog noise you hear in movies sounds the same.) Hosted on Acast.

items.title: The digital detectives preserving the tr…
items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: A lot of today’s war footage is shot on phones and posted to platforms that were never meant to permanently store it.
Digital archivist and TED Fellow Hadi Al Khatib founded Mnemonic to save these photos and videos before they vanish.
Learn how his team is turning people’s social media posts into evidence of crimes that holds up in court — and building an archive that ensures the truth outlasts the war.
(Note: this film contains disturbing footage of war.) Hosted on Acast.

items.title: Could this ancient Greek idea make us be…
items.source: TED Talks · Daily · 个人学习用
sentences: More than 2,000 years ago in ancient Athens, young citizens were required to complete “ephebeia,” a two-year civic service program that taught them the laws of the city and how to defend their democracy.
Author and historian Scott Reich believes this practice reflects something crucial we often forget: citizens aren’t born — they’re trained.
In a hopeful talk, he shares his plan to bring a modern version of this program to the United States and explains why it could benefit everyone.

sentences: Have you heard the clean energy transition is failing?
Energy analyst Michael Liebreich says to look again.
Using a four-line spreadsheet model of the global energy system, he shows why fossil fuels will inevitably get squeezed out over time — with no bans required.
The shift is well underway, he explains: it just looks different than many of us expected.
